questionsToConsider: Which task or problem are you researching? Name it in the greeting so every answer is about the same thing.
What segments do you expect, such as company size or role, and does the survey ask enough to tell them apart?
Which answers would change a product decision, and are those questions required?
How many interviews can you run, and should only certain roles be offered one?
guide.howToUseResponses: Export the answers to CSV and group respondents by role, team size and how often the task comes up. Look for clusters that share a goal and a frustration, and read their written stories side by side; those clusters are your draft personas. Use the ranking to see what each cluster values, then book interviews with a few people from each cluster to test whether the persona holds up.
customizeSteps: Replace "this kind of work" and "this task" with the specific job you are researching, such as running payroll or planning a trip.
Change the tool options to the real alternatives your users choose between today, including the manual ones.
Share the link with existing users and with people who don't use your product yet, so the personas are not only about current customers.

faqs.q: What questions should a user persona survey include?
faqs.a: Questions about role and context, the goal behind the work, how often it happens, how people do it today, what frustrates them and what they value when choosing a tool.

faqs.q: How many responses do you need to build personas?
faqs.a: Enough to see clear groups form, which depends on how varied your users are. Pair the survey with a handful of interviews per group to fill in the detail.

faqs.q: Should a persona survey use open or closed questions?
faqs.a: Both. Closed questions let you group people, and open questions about a real recent experience give you the detail personas need. The AI follow-ups in this template help when an open answer is too vague to use.

faqs.q: Can I recruit interview participants with this survey?
faqs.a: Yes. The last question asks if people are open to a call, and only those who say yes are asked for contact details.

blocks.title: Hi! We're trying to understand the people we build for. A few questions about your work and how you get it done, about four minutes.
Which of these best describes your role?
How many people work in your organisation?
What are you ultimately trying to achieve when you do this kind of work?
